_comment: Registry of Niimbot printer models and label sizes. w_px = printhead axis (width), h_px = feed axis (length). `task` selects the print-task variant in niimbot.js: "v4" (D110M/B1 Pro/B21 Pro) or "b1" (B1/B21/M2-H) — task is the protocol sequence, independent of dpi (B1 is 203 dpi, M2-H is 300 dpi, both task "b1"). `dpi` pairs a size with its model(s). `id` = printer model id for auto-detection. All models/sizes here are validated on real hardware; `_note` fields just document how a size's pixels were derived.

b2pro._note: Niimbot B2 Pro — model id 6912 (0x1B00), protocol 5, advertised name e.g. 'B2 Pro-I304050285'. Validated on hardware 2026-08-14: identifies and prints end to end, and a 3-copy job printed three labels with the printer's counter stepping page 1 → 2 → 3. protocol 'v4' is the FRAMING (0x55 0x55 ... 0xAA 0xAA); task 'v4' is the command sequence, and it is measured — the 13-byte SetPageSize (0x13→0x14) and PageEnd (0xe3→0xe4), the two commands the D110 goes silent on when driven as v4, both acked here. density 3 / label_type 1 are the values that were ACCEPTED (0x31 and 0x33 acked), not values compared against alternatives.
b2pro.label: Niimbot B2 Pro

d11h._note: Niimbot D11_H — model id 528, protocol 5, advertised name e.g. 'D11_H-H225012706'. Discovered and printed 2026-08-13; the v4 command sequence works. Printhead is 144 px, MEASURED: solid black sent at 177 px and at 144 px came out exactly the same width, so both were clipped at the same limit, while 136 px came out narrower. That also matches the value the printer itself reports in dc[03] bytes 4-5 (00 90 = 144). dpi 300 follows: 144 px over the ~12.2 mm printed band.
d11h.label: Niimbot D11_H

m2h._note: Niimbot M2-H — 300 dpi, model id 4608, protocol v4, advertised name e.g. 'M2_H-H107060027'. Validated on hardware: identifies and prints (5-label batch and single labels, 2026-08-13). Uses the b1 command sequence (per niimbluelib) with frame bundling. w_px 567 is NOT the printhead width — an earlier note said so and it is wrong: solid black at 584 printed edge to edge on this printer (2026-08-13), so the head reaches at least 584. 567 is a deliberate ~1.4 mm right margin, because THIS MODEL USES A RIBBON (thermal transfer, unlike the direct-thermal B1 Pro) and the ribbon tends to drift slightly; the margin absorbs that. Keep it unless you are testing the head itself.
m2h.label: Niimbot M2-H

d110._note: Niimbot D110 — model id 2304 (also present in the driver's INVERTED_LID_MODELS list, so niimbluelib knows this id), advertised name e.g. 'D110-FC06023035'. Validated on hardware 2026-08-14: identifies and prints end to end (printer counter reached page 1, print 100%, feed 100%). protocol 'v4' is the FRAMING (0x55 0x55 ... 0xAA 0xAA), which worked, same as every other entry; task 'b1' is the command sequence — driven as v4 the printer went silent on SetPageSize 13-byte and PageEnd, driven as b1 every command acked and the page printed. density 3 / label_type 1 are the values that were accepted (0x31 and 0x33 acked), not values compared against alternatives.
d110.label: Niimbot D110

T50x30_m2h._note: M2-H 50×30 @ 300 dpi. w_px 567 is a deliberate right margin for RIBBON DRIFT, not the printhead width — the head reaches at least 584 (solid black at 584 printed edge to edge, 2026-08-13). h_px = 30 mm × 11.81. See the m2h model note.
T50x30_m2h.label: 50 × 30 mm (M2-H)

T50x30_b2pro._note: B2 Pro 50×30 @ 300 dpi. w_px 576 is the printhead width the printer REPORTS ITSELF via probe(0xDC, [0x03]) (reply 'de' bytes 4-5 = 02 40 = 576), and 576 printed edge to edge on a 50 mm label — two independent sources agreeing, which is exactly what the M2-H's 584 lacked. h_px 354 is measured: 354 rows filled 30 mm exactly, and a 354 px wide block left ~20 mm of white beside it (at 203 dpi it would have been 44 mm and overrun). A third 300 dpi 50×30 entry is deliberate: the registry already ships T50x30 (584, B1 Pro) and T50x30_m2h (567, M2-H) for the same reason — pair a size with its MODEL, not just its dpi.
T50x30_b2pro.label: 50 × 30 mm (B2 Pro)

T15x30._note: D11_H 15×30 mm @ 300 dpi. w_px is the PRINTHEAD (144), not the label: 15 mm would be 177 px and the head clips at 144 — measured 2026-08-13 by printing solid black at 177 and at 144 and getting identical widths. So a 15 mm label keeps ~1.4 mm unprinted on each side, and that is the printer, not a choice. docs/protocol-v4.md's 136 px for this printer is wrong — 136 came out visibly narrower.
T15x30.label: 15 × 30 mm (D11_H)

T40x60._note: 40×60 @ 300 dpi, B1 Pro. Registered 2026-08-14 from a roll fitted on the maintainer's printer (tag 6972842748560, printLimit 150 / capacity 125 — 1.2, the same ratio as every other roll measured here). Geometry is arithmetic: 40 mm × 11.81 = 472, 60 mm × 11.81 = 709, and 472 is well inside the B1 Pro's head so nothing is clamped. It printed and the printer confirmed the page; nobody has yet measured the printed area against the label with a rule. NOTE ON TIME, because this is the largest size that ships. Both figures measured on a Mac 2026-08-14, where the driver paces at 10 ms/write, same label two minutes apart: the demo's REALISTIC label sent 142 row-writes, 1.7 s of upload, 4.4 s end to end; its STRESS label (corner-to-corner diagonals, which touch nearly every row and defeat run-length) sent 589 — one per row — for 6.8 s of upload and 8.6 s end to end. 4.1× the writes, 4.1× the upload. Printing itself is ~2.3 s; do not compute it by subtracting the upload, because with a slow upload the printer starts mid-stream (it was already 36% printed when the stress upload finished), so whatever follows the upload is a remainder, not the cost.
T40x60.label: 40 × 60 mm

T30x45._note: Cable flag 30×45+50 @ 300 dpi, B1 Pro. h_px covers the 45 mm FLAG ONLY, not the 50 mm transparent tail: measured 2026-08-13, the printer registers on the gap itself, so a short h_px prints the flag and still advances correctly (docs/NOTES.md § Cable flags). w_px = 30 mm × 11.81 = 354, well inside the printhead, so nothing is clamped.
T30x45.label: 30 × 45 mm (cable flag)

T25x38._note: Cable flag 25×38+40 @ 300 dpi, B1 Pro. Same convention as T30x45: h_px is the 38 mm flag, not the 40 mm tail. w_px = 25 mm × 11.81 = 295. Confirmed on paper 2026-08-13: two consecutive labels printed correctly, filling the flag with no right-edge loss, and the second registered properly — so the advance is right at this h_px too.
T25x38.label: 25 × 38 mm (cable flag)

T15x50._note: D110 15×50 mm @ 203 dpi. w_px is the PRINTHEAD (96), not the label: 15 mm at 203 dpi is 120 px; 120 px was sent and the print came out clipped at 12 mm total width (measured 2026-08-14), and 12 mm x 8 px/mm = 96, the only multiple of 8 within a millimetre of the reading (88 = 11 mm, 104 = 13 mm). So a 15 mm label keeps ~1.5 mm unprinted on each side, and that is the printer, not a choice. h_px = 400 is arithmetic from the confirmed 203 dpi (50 mm x 8), the same standing as T40x60's geometry. offset_y_px: -2 corrects PAPER REGISTRATION, not scale — h_px stays 400 because the label really is 50 mm. Measured 2026-08-14 by a six-candidate sweep printed on real hardware: six labels, each carrying its own offset drawn on it (-2, -4, -6, -8, -10, -12), compared directly against the label's physical edge — -2 is the one that came out right. This replaces an earlier single ruler reading that had indicated -6 and was wrong: that reading treated the ~0.8 mm of blank at the top as pure print offset, when a ruler comparing one label to one number can't separate offset from margin. The likely explanation, NOT confirmed — nobody has measured where the printhead actually starts reaching the label — is that part of that 0.8 mm is physical non-printable margin, not offset; correcting only 0.25 mm (the -2) leaves the rest as margin no software setting removes. Cost stands, just smaller: pulling the print up by 2 rows crops the TOP 2 rows (0.25 mm, was 0.75 mm at -6) of the source image — content drawn flush against the top edge will still be clipped. This is the first size to use a NEGATIVE offset_y_px; T50x30_b1 uses +4 (pushes down) for the opposite error on the B1, so both directions are confirmed on real hardware.
T15x50.label: 15 × 50 mm (D110)
